title: Model catalog entry contract and service-level requirements for community weights
creator: Aisha Mercado
description: Define a compact, implementable contract that each community-sourced model entry must satisfy before being enabled in the public catalog. The contract covers metadata, minimal runtime compatibility guarantees, recommended pinning policy defaults, legal/licensing checks, and a checklist for automated vs manual gating.
background: We've onboarded multiple community models with inconsistent metadata, causing runtime surprises (tokenizer mismatches, unsupported ops) and operational load. Current ad hoc reviews lead to slow turnaround and occasional production regressions. This ticket defines a predictable acceptance gate that reduces operator effort and clarifies responsibility between Model Onboarding and Runtime teams.
in_scope: metadata schema: author, license, model_id, tokenizer, vocab, default_max_length
runtime compatibility report: quantization supported, ops set, fallback path
recommended pinning policy with fallback tiers
minimal evaluation artifact: sample prompts and reference outputs
license provenance check and SPDX string
out_of_scope: full model quality evaluation at scale
performance tuning/quantization by runtime team (handled in separate ENG tickets)
automatic conversion of models between formats
acceptance_criteria: Contract document published in Confluence and linked from catalog UI
Automated linter added to intake pipeline that rejects entries missing required metadata fields
Runtime compatibility report template implemented and used by 90% of new entries during a 30-day pilot
Default pinning recommendation algorithm documented with examples for stable/staging variants
Legal team sign-off flow documented for community licenses
success_metrics: Reduction in manual review time per submission from avg 6 hours to <=2 hours
< 5% runtime incompatibility incidents from newly listed models over first 30 days
80% of community submissions pass automated checks without manual fixes during pilot
proposed_rollout_steps: Review with Runtime and Engineering (1 week)
Prototype linter rules and compatibility template (ENG)
Pilot with 10 community model submissions (2 weeks)
Iterate based on pilot, finalize Confluence doc and UI link
Enforce via pipeline and monitor metrics (30 days)
open_questions: Should we mandate a specific tokenizer serialization format (e.g., HF tokenizer.json) or allow multiple?
When license provenance is ambiguous, is manual legal review required or an automated warning acceptable?
What minimum ops set should be considered acceptable for hosted inference without significant engineering work?
notes_and_decisions: Initial decision: require HF-style tokenizer.json for pilot to reduce tokenizer mismatches
Decided to default pinning guidance to 'pin to minor version' for community models unless explicit stability claims are provided
Legal agreed that SPDX string plus link to model license is sufficient for initial acceptance; ambiguous cases are flagged for manual review
